editorial:
You just bought your dream home in Napa Valley, but the previous owner keeps showing up uninvited. That is the simple but creepy setup behind The Intruder, a thriller that plays on every homebuyer's worst nightmare. Michael Ealy and Meagan Good star as Scott and Annie, a young married couple who move into a gorgeous house on several acres, only to discover that the seller, Charlie Peck, played by Dennis Quaid, is not ready to let go. Quaid is clearly having a blast as the overly friendly, slightly unhinged former owner who keeps mowing the lawn and dropping by for dinner. The vibe is tense and uncomfortable from the start, like a neighbor who will not take a hint.

The movie shines when Quaid is on screen, turning charm into menace with a smile. Ealy and Good do solid work as the couple slowly realizing something is very wrong. The pacing keeps things moving, though some plot beats feel predictable and a few scares are telegraphed. Still, if you enjoy home-invasion thrillers with a creepy neighbor twist, this one delivers enough tension for a fun movie night.
endingExplained: In the final act, Charlie's obsession turns violent as he breaks into the house and attacks Scott and Annie. After a brutal struggle, the couple fights back and Charlie is killed, ending his grip on the property. With the threat gone, Scott and Annie survive and finally get to enjoy their new home in peace, though the experience leaves them shaken.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves home-invasion thrillers and creepy neighbor stories.
